port_difficulty.why: Sixteen lines of file plumbing, but it writes a packed decimal record it never fills, so the legacy output is not reproducible from the source alone.

blast_radius.why: Sole writer of SPARQ.TEST.MASTER, and the reader takes the layout from a second copybook, so a changed length or amount encoding breaks the read silently.

units.driving_fact: PGMW writes SPARQ.TEST.MASTER through cpy:LAYOUTX and PGMR reads it through cpy:LAYOUTY. The contract edge is medium confidence because the two copybooks are different files.

port_difficulty.why: Opens, reads one record, closes. It never touches a field, so there is nothing to transliterate.

blast_radius.why: Takes its layout from cpy:LAYOUTY, a copy of the writer's layout. A port that starts unpacking the amount could fail on data the legacy read never looked at.

units.driving_fact: PGMR reads SPARQ.TEST.MASTER as cpy:LAYOUTY but the writer used cpy:LAYOUTX. Both define 15 bytes today. Nothing keeps them equal.

port_difficulty.why: One step, but the allocation (NEW,CATLG,DELETE, one track, LRECL 80) has to be reproduced in the target, and LRECL 80 does not match the 15 byte record.

blast_radius.why: It creates the dataset the other job reads. A NEW disposition fails on a re-run unless something earlier removes the dataset, and no scheduler was supplied to show what does.

units.driving_fact: WRITEJOB allocates SPARQ.TEST.MASTER with DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE) and LRECL=80 while its program record is 15 bytes.

port_difficulty.why: One step, one shared read of an existing dataset, no DCB of its own.

blast_radius.why: Reads only, and it fails loudly if the dataset does not exist yet. The risk is order, and the order is not written down anywhere in the tree.

units.driving_fact: READJOB reads SPARQ.TEST.MASTER with DISP=SHR and is correct only after WRITEJOB has run. No scheduler artifact states that order.
